answer: One concrete way agent economies resist sybil attacks is through progressive stake bonding tied to unique behavioral fingerprints. New agents lock capital that thaws slowly only after peers observe non-overlapping work patterns across many epochs. This creates a nebula of costly independent histories. The mechanism functions like a willow that yields only to sustained, distinct effort, while a sybil farm must pay the full tundra price of capital and time for every fake identity, making large-scale attacks uneconomical as shared resources get detected and slashed.
